question: persister
prompt:
Each of your ideas must draw on a domain unrelated to the research question below, for example through an analogy, a structure, a principle, or a pattern borrowed from that domain, while still being a concrete, scientifically sound way to address the question.

Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Twin-study design for cells: barcoded sister-cell split profiling
ideas.description: Borrowing the discordant-monozygotic-twin design from epidemiology, label cells with heritable DNA barcodes, let each clone divide into sister subpopulations, then destructively profile one sister (scRNA-seq/ATAC) while drugging the other, and use the barcode to retroactively assign the pre-treatment molecular state of cells whose twins survived. This directly tests whether survival is predictable from a pre-existing transcriptional/chromatin state rather than a post-hoc drug response.

ideas.title: Foreshock detection: long-term live imaging for precursor dynamics and lead time
ideas.description: Treat rare survival like a rare earthquake and apply seismology's foreshock analysis: image cells for days before and during treatment with multiplexed live reporters (e.g., ERK/AKT kinase translocation sensors, NF-κB, stress and cell-cycle reporters), then align single-cell traces retrospectively to the survival outcome. Fitting the hazard of survival to the preceding signaling history yields both the identity of precursor signatures and the characteristic 'lead time' over which the predisposed state exists.

ideas.title: Ensemble forecasting: measuring the memory timescale of the surviving state
ideas.description: Adapt the predictability/autocorrelation-decay analysis of weather and climate forecasting by isolating single cells, expanding them for variable numbers of generations, and re-challenging replicate subcultures with drug at each time point. The decay of correlation in survival fraction between sibling subcultures as a function of elapsed divisions quantifies how many generations the resistant state is inherited, cleanly separating transient fluctuation, epigenetic memory, and genetic mutation.

ideas.title: Per-cell dosimetry: ruling out pharmacological escape before invoking cell state
ideas.description: Following occupational radiation safety, where every worker wears a personal dosimeter, measure the drug dose each individual cell actually receives and engages, using a fluorescent or clickable drug analog, MALDI/nanoSIMS imaging of the unlabeled compound, efflux-pump reporters, and single-cell target-engagement readouts (phospho-target staining or in-cell thermal shift). This distinguishes survivors that are genuinely drug-tolerant from those that merely experienced a low effective dose because of uptake, efflux, or target abundance differences.

ideas.title: Ice cores and tree rings: DNA-based molecular recorders that write signaling history
ideas.description: Use CRISPR base-editor or recombinase recording systems driven by pathway-responsive promoters so that each cell continuously inscribes a cumulative, timestamped proxy record of its signaling and stress history into its own genome, analogous to paleoclimate proxies in ice layers. Sequencing the recorder locus in the rare survivors after treatment recovers their multi-day history even though they were never destructively sampled, revealing whether survivors came from cells with distinctive prior pathway activity.
